equity_bridge.item: Standard Life plc (ex-Phoenix) ~10% stake at fair value
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim p.11 and Note 17 (FY2025: GBP767m). Its GBP29m half-year dividend is an adjusting item outside AOP, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule). Excluded from regulatory own funds. Listed and liquid, but would mark down with equity markets in the bear case.

equity_bridge.item: Debt securities held as corporate liquid resources, net of restricted cash
equity_bridge.note: Ties the bridge to the company's own 'cash and liquid resources' GBP1.6bn (H1 2026 APM reconciliation: GBP1.3bn IFRS cash + GBP0.4bn debt securities - GBP0.1bn collateral/EBT/charitable cash). Seed capital (GBP115m) excluded.

equity_bridge.item: HASL (China JV) and other associates at equity book
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 Note 10. Share of profit (GBP11m H1 2026) is excluded from AOP, so the carrying value enters the bridge.

equity_bridge.item: DB pension surplus: PV of the DC-contribution offset management is extracting
equity_bridge.note: GBP38m/yr (H1 2026: GBP19m 'utilisation of DB surplus to fund DC benefits', added in the NCG reconciliation because AOP charges the full DC cost) for ten years at 9.5% = GBP239m. The residual GBP0.8bn IAS19 surplus is not credited: trustee consent, 25% refund tax, buyout-basis gap.
GBP11m/yr coupon is paid as a distribution outside AOP; instrument to be redeemed from cash at first call in December 2026 (subject to FCA approval). Deducted at par.

equity_bridge.item: Regulatory capital lock-up haircut on the Own Funds Threshold Requirement
equity_bridge.note: OFTR GBP834m at 30 Jun 2026 must be permanently retained as own funds and earns roughly the gilt yield (already excluded from AOP). Credited at the PV of that yield at the cost of equity (4.5%/10.3% = 44% of par) rather than at par: 834 x (1 - 0.44) = -470. Own funds above the OFTR are credited in full through net cash; management's 140-180% coverage target implies they will hold more than this, used to retire Tier 2 debt (deducted at par in net_debt).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward segment blend, not a historical CAGR: ii growing ~15%+ (27% of revenue), Investments roughly -1% to flat (56%), Adviser flat (16%) gives ~4% near term fading to 2%; cross-checked against management's medium-term net capital generation growth target of 5-10% p.a. beyond FY2026 (which includes margin expansion).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (-6.3%) and revenue (-2.6%) 5-year CAGRs are negative while adjusted operating profit compounded +3.8%: the book-value and revenue history is distorted by the Phoenix stake sell-downs, the sale of the insurance and financial-planning businesses, GBP1.5bn of 2019-2023 buybacks/capital returns and FY2022 fair-value losses. Neither backward CAGR is a usable forward anchor; the model is anchored on FY2026 guidance and the segment mix instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 -63, FY2021 -63, FY2022 +21, FY2023 +53, FY2024 +61, FY2025 +300. The FY2025 jump reflects a one-off surge in operating cash flow (consolidated-fund, collateral and pension-related movements), not operating improvement, so no FCF CAGR is reported. EPS 3-year CAGR is undefined (FY2022 EPS was -26.6p). Metrics in GBP millions from ABDN.L_Metrics.csv / dcf-context.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 targets met; ii compounds, Investments flows stabilise near zero, Adviser inflows return a year late; gradual BoE cuts offset by growing ii balances; AOP margin 21.5% -> 25% by FY2031; revenue growth 4% fading to 2%.
scenario_narratives.bull: All three segments turn together - ii 15%+ growth, Adviser >GBP1bn FY2027 inflows, Investments net inflows on CEF/private markets - with rates higher for longer; AOP margin to 28%; top of the 5-10% NCG growth range.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rate cuts compress ii treasury income by GBP60-70m, Adviser and Investments outflows persist, a 2027 market drawdown clips revenue 3%; AOP margin falls to 17-17.5% (FY2023-24 levels). Earnings bear, not solvency: coverage stays >180%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Aberdeen as a fee-based operating company on owner FCF built from adjusted operating profit, then add - item by item - the non-operating assets whose income the company itself excludes from AOP (Standard Life plc stake, liquid resources, HASL, the extractable slice of the pension surplus) and deduct the claims ahead of ordinary shareholders (Tier 2 notes, AT1 notes) and the capital the regulator will never let out. Roughly 38% of the market cap is balance sheet rather than earnings, so the bridge is shown line by line for a reader to challenge. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights; WACC is the same in all three cases.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate path: ii treasury income (GBP161m FY2025, ~55% of ii revenue growth) scales with BoE base rate; each 50bp of cash margin on GBP8.6bn of balances is ~GBP43m of pre-tax profit.
Flows: Investments (ex-liquidity) and Adviser remain in net outflow; the Adviser >GBP1bn FY2027 inflow target has already slipped once.
Equity markets: fee revenue and the GBP867m Standard Life plc stake both move with markets; the bridge is marked at 30 Jun 2026 and is scenario-independent in the engine.

Bridge judgments: the -GBP470m regulatory lock-up haircut and the +GBP239m pension-offset credit are stated assumptions worth ~26p and ~13p per share respectively; crediting cash at par and the full surplus would add ~40p, deducting the whole OFTR at par would remove ~20p.

Capital allocation: GBP1.5bn of buybacks in 2019-2023 bought at prices well above today's; a return to buybacks would be accretive at 243p but management has prioritised debt reduction and bolt-on M&A.
Execution: multi-year transformation with recurring leadership change; FY2026 target depends on an H2 step-up (H1 AOP GBP151m vs GBP300m full year).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (ABDN.L) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 179.6-265.0 GBp.
data_sources.financials: ABDN.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2019-H1 FY2026); ABDN.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (balance sheet, capital base, Note 7 diluted shares, Note 10 associates, APM reconciliations, lease cash flows); ABDN.L_Annual_FY2025.txt (AOP by segment, D&A inside adjusted opex GBP29m, SBC, tax on adjusted profit, lease liabilities).
data_sources.qualitative: ABDN.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): segment mix, guidance as of H1 2026 results 29 Jul 2026, bull/bear axes.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 adjusted net operating revenue (AR FY2025 p.~2004). H1 2026 was GBP677m (+3% YoY); Y1 of the model is FY2026.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted ordinary shares, H1 2026 interim Note 7 (1,832m; basic 1,793m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows and the employee benefit trusts buy shares in the market (GBP34m FY2025) to settle awards, so the count does not compound.
inputs.sbc_source: AR FY2025 cash flow statement, 'Equity settled share-based payments' GBP28m (2024: GBP26m); no separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed (UK awards are settled through employee benefit trusts), so EquityAwardTaxes is 0 and sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc.
inputs.buyback_note: No formal buyback programme in FY2024-FY2025 (last was GBP302m in FY2023). GBP34m is the FY2025 financing outflow for shares acquired by employee benefit trusts, which is the mechanism that keeps the count flat against SBC grants.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 is the engine's model->quote rate (GBP/share x 100 = pence/share). quote_currency is written GBX - the ISO-style alias for pence sterling that sanity_check.py, refresh_price.py and canonical_iv.py all map to GBp - because scripts/dcf_engine.py upper()-folds 'GBp' into 'GBP', sees no currency difference and skips the conversion (per-share values then print as 2.83 'GBp' instead of 283). ENGINE LIMITATION for a maintainer: dcf_engine should keep GBp distinct from GBP (it is 1/100 GBP); until then GBX is the only spelling that yields pence headline values. Yahoo reports the ABDN.L quote currency as GBp. Fixed definitional conversion, no market rate and no dual listing to parity-check.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: 10y gilt ~4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta 1.15 (UK asset managers/platforms, market-sensitive fee base) = cost of equity ~10.3%; GBP564m Tier 2 notes at ~6% pre-tax / 4.5% post-tax, ~12% of EV; WACC 9.5%. Identical across scenarios: cyclicality, rate sensitivity and flow risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate. Terminal growth 2.0% (UK nominal growth less structural fee compression); terminal cap 14x owner FCF for a mature, cyclical, fee-based financial (Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% = 13.6x, so Gordon binds).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease principal + interest (FY2025: GBP16m + GBP5m = GBP21m, 1.5% of revenue; H1 2026 GBP13m + GBP2m) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (GBP155m at FY2025) EXCLUDED from total_debt; da_pct_path is depreciation and software amortisation EX right-of-use depreciation (~GBP16m of the GBP29m D&A inside adjusted operating expenses). ebitda_margin_path is therefore AOP margin + SBC 2.1pp + ROU depreciation ~1.1pp + da_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Ordinary-share NCI is negligible (GBP1m). The GBP6m/half AT1 coupon ('interest paid on other equity') is the only material non-ordinary claim: it is excluded from AOP and the GBP210m AT1 instrument is deducted at par in the equity bridge (charged once, in the bridge).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company route, with the non-US adaptations: GBP WACC, single lease treatment, matching-asset bridge). Aberdeen is a fee-based operating company (ii D2C platform ~27% of revenue, Adviser platform ~16%, Investments asset management ~56%), not a bank, insurer or holdco: it has no deposit funding, no float, and its own primary metric (net capital generation) is an owner-cash concept. REVENUE/PROFIT BASE: the component build runs off adjusted net operating revenue and adjusted operating profit (AOP), which exclude corporate interest income, Standard Life plc dividends, HASL associate profit, pension net interest credit, the AT1 coupon, restructuring/transaction costs and acquired-intangible amortisation (GBP102m FY2025, non-cash and not economic for a going concern). Reported FCF (OCF GBP427m less capex GBP21m = GBP406m FY2025) is NOT a usable base: OCF is inflated by consolidated-fund, collateral and pension-related movements; last_fcf = 406 - 28 - 78 = 300 is recorded for the contract, but the Y1 owner FCF the engine produces (~GBP220m) is the component-built figure on FY2026 guidance (AOP >= GBP300m, reaffirmed 29 Jul 2026). CASH TAX: adjusted ETR 22% but cash tax paid only GBP21m FY2025 / GBP22m H1 2026 (historic unrecognised losses, DTAs GBP151m); ramped 12% -> 25% over six years. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture -25% on revenue change models the Own Funds Threshold Requirement growing with the business (K-factor/fixed-overhead based) - growth consumes regulatory capital. BRIDGE (30 Jun 2026): net cash GBP781m (cash 1,345 less Tier 2 notes 564) plus the itemised equity_bridge, net +GBP929m; the bridge is ~38% of market cap at 243p, so the valuation is unusually sensitive to how non-operating assets are credited - each item is stated so a reader can zero it. The regulatory lock-up haircut (-GBP470m, ~26p/share) is a judgment: the GBP834m OFTR must be retained forever and earns ~gilt yield, so it is credited at the PV of that yield at the cost of equity (~44% of par) instead of par. Seed capital and co-investments (~GBP115m+) are NOT credited (conservative; not separately quantified in the interim). The residual GBP0.8bn IAS19 pension surplus is NOT credited beyond the DC-funding offset. In the bear case the Standard Life plc stake (GBP867m, listed) would also mark down; the engine's bridge is scenario-independent, so the bear IV is overstated by perhaps 10-15p in a 2008-style drawdown. FILINGS: ABDN.L_Annual_FY2026.txt is a byte-identical duplicate of ABDN.L_Annual_FY2025.txt (md5 145ffa2b...) and HalfYear_H2-2026.txt duplicates H1-2026.txt - both mislabelled copies, not new filings; the parser should drop them. SCENARIOS share WACC/terminal; risk is in the flows and weights.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: AOP margin [20.5, 18.0, 17.0, 17.0, 17.5, 17.5, 17.5, 17.5, 17.5, 17.5] + 3.2pp + da_pct_path. FY2026 AOP lands ~GBP280m (target missed), then falls to ~GBP225m as treasury income compresses and outflows persist.
bear.narrative: The two legacy businesses keep bleeding and the rate tailwind reverses. BoE cuts take ii's cash margin from 234bps toward 150bps (c.GBP60-70m of high-margin treasury income lost); Adviser's return to inflows slips again and Investments' equities and insurance-partner run-off outpace the closed-end-fund bolt-ons; a 2027 equity market drawdown takes 3% off group revenue. Cost savings are already in the base, so the AOP margin falls back to 17-17.5%, roughly FY2023-24 profitability, and the dividend is covered only thinly. No solvency question - capital coverage stays above 180% - so this is an earnings bear, not a balance-sheet one; the Standard Life plc stake in the bridge would also mark down (not modelled; see inputs.notes).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Equals adjusted operating profit margin [21.5, 22.5, 23.3, 24.0, 24.5, 25.0, 25.0, 25.0, 25.0, 25.0] + SBC 2.1pp + ROU depreciation 1.1pp + da_pct_path. Y1 ties to FY2026 guidance of AOP >= GBP300m on ~GBP1,395m revenue. Mature 25% AOP margin: transformation programme (GBP180m+ annualised savings) complete end-2026, ii cost/AUMA < 18bps and mix shift toward ii (~50% segment margin) offset by gradual BoE rate cuts compressing ii treasury income.
base.capex_note: H1 2026 capex ran GBP32m (GBP27m capitalised software for Adviser Wrap insourcing and ii 360), ~4.7% of H1 revenue, vs GBP21m FY2025 (1.6%); elevated through the platform build then converging on D&A at 1.8% (steady state).
base.narrative: FY2026 targets met (AOP >= GBP300m, NCG c.GBP300m). ii keeps compounding customers ~12-14% a year and holds the flat-fee share gains; Investments flows stabilise near zero as closed-end-fund bolt-ons and real assets offset insurance-partner run-off; Adviser returns to modest inflows in 2027-28, a year later than guided. BoE cuts trim ii's cash margin from 234bps but growing balances hold treasury income roughly flat. Group revenue grows ~4% fading to 2%; AOP margin reaches 25% by FY2031 and holds.

bull.narrative: The turnaround lands on all three axes at once: ii sustains 15%+ customer growth and SIPP share gains with brand awareness past 40%; Adviser hits the >GBP1bn FY2027 net-inflow target under Rich Denning; Investments turns to net inflows on closed-end funds, private markets and emerging markets with 86% of AUM outperforming; UK rates stay higher for longer, keeping treasury income growing. Operating leverage lifts the AOP margin to 28% (still below pure platform peers HL/AJ Bell at 45-55%, reflecting the Investments mix) and management delivers the top of its 5-10% NCG growth range.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right (Adviser flows, Investments flows, rates staying high) and management has already pushed out the Adviser target once. Bear lifted to 25% because two of three segments are in persistent net outflow and ii's largest profit driver is treasury income on an interest-rate path the company does not control - but not higher, because there is no solvency or refinancing risk (229% capital coverage, GBP400m undrawn RCF) and the bear is an earnings case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: sanity_check.py's historical_table multiplied the GBp (pence) price series by fx_rate=100 instead of dividing -- the quote->reporting vs reporting->quote direction conflict documented in sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict.md (7th occurrence, same shape as AAF.L). Printed P/B up to 11,866x and P/Sales up to 44,688x, which is nonsense, not a real trip. Forced passed:false here because an automated pass built on garbage inputs is worse than a automated fail -- see sanity_check_note for the hand-bridged multiples, which are a genuine pass.

sanity_check_note.reason: scripts/sanity_check.py divides reporting-currency book value/EPS by a GBp price series multiplied (not divided) by fx_rate=100, producing historical multiples off by ~100x (P/B up to 11,866x, P/S up to 44,688x). Hand-bridged below by converting the pence price series to GBP (divide by 100) and comparing against FY-end book value and revenue in GBP millions, both already consistent units. See [[sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict]].
sanity_check_note.verdict: genuine pass -- implied P/B (1.00x) and P/S (3.67x) at the weighted IV both sit within the hand-bridged 10yr historical range (P/B 0.53-1.19x, P/S 1.85-4.47x). No driver changes made.
